holidays.name: National Greasy Foods Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to indulging in fried, oily, and gloriously messy comfort food. Think french fries, doughnuts, onion rings, and burgers dripping with goodness. Napkins are strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday of unclear origin, popularized by food-observance calendars and restaurants that love an excuse to promote their fried menu items.
holidays.funFact: The word 'greasy spoon' for a cheap diner dates back to at least the early 1900s and refers to the less-than-pristine silverware and the heavy fried fare.

holidays.name: World Pasta Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of pasta in all its shapes and sauces, from spaghetti and penne to farfalle and rigatoni. Pasta lovers around the world twirl, slurp, and carb-load in unity.
holidays.origin: Established in 1995 at the World Pasta Congress in Rome, organized by the International Pasta Organisation to celebrate pasta as a healthy, affordable, and universal food.
holidays.funFact: Italy has over 300 documented pasta shapes, and the average Italian eats around 51 pounds (23 kg) of pasta per year.

holidays.name: Pablo Picasso's Birthday
holidays.description: Art fans celebrate the birthday of the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism and made faces with two noses and three eyes look like genius. Some people mark the day by doodling wonky portraits.
holidays.origin: Pablo Picasso was born October 25, 1881, in Málaga, Spain, and went on to become one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.
holidays.funFact: Picasso's full name has 23 words, beginning with Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan Nepomuceno María de los Remedios Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso.

holidays.name: Punk for a Day Day
holidays.description: A day to unleash your inner rebel with spiky hair, safety pins, leather jackets, and loud music. Participants are encouraged to dress in punk style and crank up the volume, at least until the neighbors complain.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created by fans of punk culture, with the date placed in the fall when mohawks and ripped plaid blend nicely with Halloween costume planning.
holidays.funFact: The Ramones played only about 2,263 concerts over 22 years, and their signature look of ripped jeans and leather jackets became the template for punk fashion.

holidays.name: Sourest Day
holidays.description: A tongue-puckering celebration of all things sour, from lemon drops and sour gummy worms to pickles and tart candies. Brave souls take on face-scrunching sour challenges.
holidays.origin: An unofficial candy and snack observance, promoted by novelty holiday calendars that mark the season of sour candy as Halloween approaches.
holidays.funFact: Humans have about 2,000 to 8,000 taste buds, and sour taste exists partly as a warning system to detect unripe or spoiled food.
